review_notes: I read the whole file. It has no @[simp] declarations, no simp sets, and no simp-driven proofs. Its only `simp`-adjacent tactics are `dsimp [Budget.sourceSize, ...]`, `unfold ...; ring`, and `convert ... using 1` followed by `rfl`. The new definitions (`Budget.sourceSize`, `baseCorrectionSize`, `sourceCost`, `pressureCost`, `timeDerivativeCost`) are bound-bookkeeping constants. Their intended use is as opaque names that get unfolded once by `unfold` and `ring`. I checked downstream uses in PacketForwardUniformBudget.lean (lines 117–126) and BaseEulerState.lean (lines 1600–1607). They match these costs against other constants by `rfl` and `rw`, not by simp. So I found no evidence that a simp lemma, an orientation change, or an attribute would help any real use. Adding @[simp] to `pressureCost` or `timeDerivativeCost` would only expand the constants into the large `(B.spatial q hq).full…` expressions. That would be an unwanted expansion. I found no competing rules and no credible rewrite cycle. I could not run Lean, so I only judged the simp interface by reading the code.
